title: Microsoft Teams: advanced collaboration analytics for GCC
summary: Pass: the roadmap facts, control paths, Graph operation and existing-feature licensing are supported, and the briefing distinguishes those documents from the planned GCC release. Minor corrections should clarify the reports setting's documented reach and remove a checklist instruction whose control is not in the table.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans advanced collaboration analytics for GCC with insights covering teams, federated domains, channels, guests and internal users.
claims.quote: Advanced Collaboration Analytics for GGC provides Teams admins with insights into external collaboration patterns - covering teams, federated domains, channels, guests, and internal users

claims.claim: The roadmap promises recommended actions to enhance security for external collaboration.
claims.quote: along with recommended actions to enhance security for external collaboration.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: An API or automation surface for the Collaboration activity dashboard is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Collaboration activity" "advanced collaboration analytics" Graph API PowerShell reports' and '"Collaboration activity" "Teams PowerShell" analytics API'; read the feature page and Graph/PowerShell search excerpts. Results describe other usage reports, not this dashboard.

claims.claim: The concealment setting is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org Settings > Services > Reports > Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote:
select **Settings**.
Select [Org Settings]
On the **Services** tab, select **Reports**.
In the **Reports** panel, uncheck the checkbox next to **Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports**.

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/admin/reportSettings updates the tenant reports setting.
claims.quote:
Update tenant-level settings for Microsoft 365 reports.
PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/admin/reportSettings

claims.claim: The request body property displayConcealedNames determines concealment.
claims.quote: displayConcealedNames | Boolean | If set to `true`, all reports conceal user information such as usernames, groups, and sites. If `false`, all reports show identifiable information.

claims.claim: The organization-wide reports concealment setting governs revealing data in the collaboration cards and applies to Teams admin center usage reports.
claims.quote:
Other reports, such as some reports in the Microsoft Teams admin center, follow this organization setting.
This setting also applies to the Microsoft 365 usage reports in [Microsoft Graph] and [Power BI] and to [the usage reports in Microsoft Teams Admin center].

claims.claim: The correctly documented general reports setting is marked as not confirmed for GCC.
claims.quote: Admins can use an API in all environments to change this setting without needing to visit the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.fix: Replace 'Not confirmed for GCC.' with 'The usage reports page documents changing this organization setting by API in all environments; the GCC collaboration dashboard itself remains a planned release.'

claims.claim: The usage reports page identifies Global administrators as able to change the UI setting to display concealed information.
claims.quote: Global administrators can update the settings to display concealed information if your organization's privacy practices allow it.

claims.claim: Showing identifiable user information is logged in the Microsoft Purview portal audit log.
claims.quote: Showing identifiable user information is a logged event in the Microsoft Purview portal audit log.
